Theme

Church life

hell noun

the place of the damned

also go to hell, the underworld, Hades, the fires of hell

late Latin

Vulg. Ps. 9.18; Job 17.13; Ambr. in Psalm. 48.22 (Lewis & Short)

īnfernus, īnfernī m.

noun, second declension

(vōx ecclēsiastica: Vulg., Ambr.)

The adjective īnfernus, lower, of the world below, made a noun in the Church’s Latin: Lewis & Short, “hell (eccl. Lat.)”. It is the everyday Church word for hell.

Other words

  • gehenna, gehennae f. — hell, the place of punishment

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Mt. 5.22; 10.28; 18.9 (Lewis & Short); Aug. Conf. 11.12.14

    (vōx ecclēsiastica: Vulg., Tert., Prud.)

    Hebrew Ge-Hinnom, a valley by Jerusalem where children were sacrificed to Moloch; in the Gospels the hell of fire (Lewis & Short).

  • īnferī, īnferōrum m. pl. — the dead; the world below

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 12: ad superōs … deōs potius quam ad īnferōs pervēnisse (Lewis & Short); Ambr. hymn. Intende 23: excursus ūsque ad īnferōs

    Classically the dead and the world below them (Lewis & Short, s.v. inferus). In Ambrose’s hymn Christ goes down ad īnferōs, to the dead, not to the hell of the damned.

Examples

  • ‘alta,’ inquit, ‘scrūtantibus gehennās parābat’

    “He was making hell,” he said, “for people who pry into deep things”Aug. Conf. 11.12.14

  • ēgressus ejus ā Patre, regressus ejus ad Patrem, excursus ūsque ad īnferōs, recursus ad sēdem Deī

    his going out from the Father, his return to the Father, his journey down to the dead, his way back to the throne of GodAmbr. hymn. Intende 21–24

See also heaven, sin, soul, God.
